Indicator (units): Bottom temperature (annual prior to Fall and Spring surveys, °C)
Recent Status: Near the long term mean (fall and spring)
Implications: Since 2023, annual mean temperatures prior to the fall survey (top; October - September, bottom; March - February) have declined from recent highs and are near the long-term mean. An overall warming trend in bottom temperatures may eventually result in changes in plaice distribution and condition. Bottom water temperatures control spawning - optimum spawning temperatures range between 3-6C but can thrive from -0.5 to 13C. Spring bottom temperatures are also correlated with mean latitude of plaice distribution. This data set does not yet include 2026.

Indicator (units): Gulf Stream Index (annual mean prior to Fall survey)
Implications: The annual mean of the Gulf Stream position leading up to fall survey affects recruitment. When the strength of Labrador current is weak, a higher proportion of warm water coming from the Gulf Stream enters the Gulf of Maine, increasing Gulf of Maine water temperatures. There is an overall long-term increasing trend in the position of the Gulf Stream since 1970, with the Gulf Stream being further north than the long-term mean in the 2010s, which may be contributing to warmer water temperatures in the Gulf of Maine and affecting plaice recruitment.

March-June SST anomaly affects plaice recruitment, as the thermal limit for survival and incubation of American plaice eggs is 14C. Spring temperatures have hovered around 7-8°C since the early 1980s, however temperatures in the early 2020s exceeded the long-term mean. Seasonal temperatures have declined since 2022, which may be beneficial for plaice recruitment. However, a long-term increasing trend in sea surface temperatures may lead to overall declines in recruitment.

Indicator (units): AMO (6 months prior to Fall and Spring survey)
Recent Status: Above the long term mean (fall and spring)
Implications: The AMO index has been above the long-term mean since 2020. AMO values below 0 and above 0.25 are associated with lower recruitment, while values between approximately 0-0.25 are associated with higher recruitment (Behan and Kerr 2022, fig. 2). Recent AMO values are positive, with some being above the transition point of ~0.25, so impacts on recruitment may be mixed.
